title: Peppers, banana or Hungarian wax, seeded, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Banana pepper (also known as Hungarian wax) is a sweet, seedless variety of Capsicum annuum eaten raw. It has a bright yellow‑orange color, crisp texture, and a mildly sweet, slightly fruity flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the fruit’s banana‑like shape.
Hungarian wax is popular in Eastern European cuisine as a milder alternative to hot peppers.
The seedless variety is convenient for cooking and child‑friendly.
High in carotenoids, which give the pepper its vivid hue.
In North America it is often sold as “sweet banana peppers.”

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Provides about 100 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids such as beta‑carotene and lycopene help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Approximately 20 kcal per 100 g, making it a diet‑friendly snack.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Supports protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium for heart health
items.content: Helps regulate blood pressure and supports cardiac function.

items.title: Pepper allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as itching, swelling, or hives.

items.title: Foodborne contamination
items.content: Raw peppers can harbor bacteria if not stored properly; rinse thoroughly before eating.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts may cause gas or stomach upset in people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat banana peppers fresh in salads, sandwiches, as a snack with dip, or add them to fresh rolls. They are also used in pickles and stuffed dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 1 week. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 3 months.
